summary: Both retained estimates were independently checked against the paper. Read the complete 60,226-character markdown conversion in four contiguous chunks, through references and end matter. The supplied PDF has 10 pages and no appended or embedded supplement. Extracted PDF text with PyMuPDF for all estimate source pages (5, 6 and 7), and methods/supporting pages 3, 4 and 10; also inspected in-memory rendered crops of the flagged mathematical passages on pages 5 and 6. All six mechanical warnings are false positives caused by PDF mathematical-font text encoding, line wrapping and subscript tokenization. On PDF p. 5, the objective expert-rated comparison explicitly prints human M = 2.311, s.d. = 0.469; LLM M = 2.45, s.d. = 0.453; t with df 202 = −2.154; P = 0.032; d = −0.301; and 95% CI (−0.266, −0.012). These values belong to objective creativity, despite appearing under the Self-reported creativity heading. The negative t and d are transcribed correctly in the paper’s human-minus-LLM order, as the extraction explains. The CI estimand and d standardizer are not explicitly identified, so the extraction appropriately avoids assigning or deriving them. On PDF p. 6, the objective-creativity LLM-response-type main effect prints F with numerator df 1 and denominator df 200 = 0.811, P = 0.369, and partial eta squared = 0.004. The printed punctuation and numbers agree with the retained quotation after mathematical notation is linearized. The eta2 schema label is qualified as partial eta squared. No pooled signed effect, arm means, SDs or arm counts are printed for this contrast. The Fig. 2 and Fig. 4 captions on PDF pp. 6 and 7 respectively explicitly print N = 204 for the analyzed samples. Recruitment and random assignment are described on pp. 4 and 5. Null arm counts are appropriate; no count was inferred from degrees of freedom or assumed balanced allocation. The pooled arm names match the screening form and the experimental conditions. Both outcomes are expert-rated overall creativity, with_ai, measured immediately while supplied partner ideas are available, with higher values indicating more creativity. The between-participant designs justify within_person = null. Participant scores and participant-level analyses support unit = participant, se_basis = participant and S1 sd_level = participant. S1 correctly compares AI with an active human partner; S2 correctly treats the proposed constrained-responsive configuration as treatment against batch-responsive LLM. No additional eligible full-sample outcome/contrast was found in the supplied article. Task-conditional simple effects and mediation/moderation results are excluded by rules 4–5; the additional S1 ANOVAs test the already retained outcome/contrast/sample. Self-reports, manipulation checks and stimulus-pool ratings are outside scope. Expert-rated fixation compares participant ideas with supplied LLM ideas, not across different participants, and the article reports only conditional treatment-to-fixation effects. Participant fluency has no reported full-sample contrast. Coverage limitation: external supplementary Tables S5–S8 could not be checked. No matching local supplement was located; urllib requests with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to the publisher article and the OSF project files API both failed with WinError 10013 socket-access restrictions. The empty problems list confirms the retained estimates and completeness within the supplied article; it does not certify unavailable supplementary material. No unverified supplementary counts or results were guessed.
